name: useEffect cleanup
desc: The function returned from an effect runs before the next run and on unmount. It cancels timers, subscriptions, and stale requests.

name: useReducer
desc: Moves state transitions into one pure function. It pays off when several fields change together or the next state depends on the previous one.
body:
## Why a reducer

With `useState` every rule about the next value lives in an event handler. A reducer collects those rules in one function that can be read and tested on its own.

## The rules

- The reducer must be pure. Return a new object, never mutate `state`.
- Every action goes through `dispatch`, so logging one place shows all changes.
- An unknown action should throw in development, not silently return the old state.
- `useReducer` is not only for large state. Three related fields are enough.

name: useMemo
desc: Caches a computed value between renders until a dependency changes. Use it for expensive work, not for every variable.

name: useCallback
desc: Keeps the same function identity between renders while dependencies stay equal. It matters when a memoized child receives the function.

name: useContext
desc: Reads the nearest provider value without prop drilling. The component re-renders when that value changes.

name: useRef for DOM nodes
desc: Holds a mutable reference that survives renders. Attached to an element, ref.current points at the DOM node after mount.

name: useId
desc: Produces a stable id that matches between server and client render. Use it to link labels and inputs instead of hardcoded ids.

name: useTransition
desc: Marks a state update as non urgent, so typing stays responsive while a heavy list re-renders.

name: useDeferredValue
desc: Returns a lagging copy of a value. The UI keeps the old copy while the expensive part renders the new one.

name: useLayoutEffect
desc: Runs after the DOM is updated but before the browser paints. Use it to measure or reposition, never for data fetching.

name: React.memo
desc: Skips a re-render when props are shallowly equal. It helps only when the parent renders often and the props are stable.

name: forwardRef
desc: Passes a ref through a function component to a DOM node. React 19 accepts ref as a normal prop, older versions need this wrapper.

name: React.lazy and Suspense
desc: Splits a component into its own chunk and loads it on demand. Suspense shows a fallback while the chunk downloads.

name: createPortal
desc: Renders children into another DOM node while keeping React context and event bubbling. It is how modals escape overflow and z-index traps.

name: Error boundary
syntax: class Boundary extends Component { static getDerivedStateFromError() {} }
desc: Catches render errors in its subtree and shows a fallback. There is no hook version, so it stays a class component.

name: Custom hook: useFetch
syntax: function useFetch(url) { ... return { data, error, loading }; }
desc: A custom hook is a function that calls other hooks and returns state. This one fetches JSON and cancels stale requests.

name: Context provider with a guard
syntax: export function useAuth() { const ctx = useContext(AuthContext); ... }
desc: Wraps useContext in a custom hook that throws when no provider is above. That turns a silent undefined into a clear error.
